summary: ukraine69 harvests Telegram session vaults and deletes victim accounts at import time
details: On import, ukraine69 enumerates Telegram/Hotaru session vault files across the user's environment (HOTARU_ACCOUNT_ROOT/HOTARU_ACCOUNT_SESSION env hints, ~/.hotaru, ~/.local/share/hotaru, ~/.config/hotaru, cwd ancestors, recursive ~/**/*.vault glob, /run and /tmp/hotaru*). For each vault, it extracts the MTProto auth_key, api_id, and api_hash and spawns a detached isolated Python interpreter (subprocess.Popen([sys.executable,'-I','-c', <generated payload>], start_new_session=True)) that initializes the goygram TL schema, injects the stolen auth_key into an MTProto session against hardcoded Telegram DC IPs (149.154.175.53, 149.154.167.51, 149.154.175.100, 149.154.167.91, 91.108.56.130), performs the SRP auth.checkPassword flow when a 2FA password is stored, and invokes account.deleteAccount (with DeleteAccountRequest as fallback) to destroy the victim's Telegram account. On success, the vault and.session files are unlinked. A secondary garbage-collection script recursively wipes the package and its dist-info from ~/.cache/hotaru/module-deps, pip wheel and http-v2 caches, ~/.cache/uv, $TMPDIR/probe-*, and every resolved site-packages directory, with a second pass to defeat reinstall. The module docstring self-identifies as a Hotaru sandbox-escape payload.
